downgrade:acc-hardware-lsm6dsv16x-not-in.detail: PR #13046 added LSM6DSV16X support to the accelerometer hardware list after 4.4.3, so 4.4.3 doesn't accept that name.
downgrade:acc-hardware-lsm6dsv16x-not-in.note: 4.4.3 has no driver for the LSM6DSV16X, so the accelerometer is set back to `set acc_hardware = AUTO`, which uses whatever sensor 4.4.3 detects. After flashing, check that the accelerometer is detected and working before you rely on angle or horizon mode.

downgrade:acc-hardware-virtual-renamed-f.detail: PR #12493 renamed the FAKE accelerometer entry to VIRTUAL with no change in function. 4.4.3 still uses the old name.
downgrade:acc-hardware-virtual-renamed-f.note: The accelerometer choice VIRTUAL is called FAKE in 4.4.3, so your value was renamed to match. It works the same way and you don't need to do anything.

downgrade:angle-limit-renamed-to-level-l.detail: PR #12231 renamed level_limit (10-90) to angle_limit (10-85) without changing what it means: the maximum angle in degrees at full stick in Angle mode. Every 4.5.5 value is also valid in 4.4.3.
downgrade:angle-limit-renamed-to-level-l.note: Your Angle mode maximum tilt angle carries over with the same value in degrees, under its 4.4.3 name. Nothing to do.

downgrade:baro-hardware-new-sensors-not-.detail: PR #13054 added the LPS22DF barometer and PR #12493 introduced the VIRTUAL name, both after 4.4.3, so 4.4.3 accepts neither name.
downgrade:baro-hardware-new-sensors-not-.note: 4.4.3 doesn't support this barometer choice, so your board's own 4.4.3 barometer default is used instead. If you use the barometer, check that it is detected after flashing; otherwise there is nothing to do.

downgrade:debug-mode-new-modes-not-in-ta.detail: The debug modes ANGLE_MODE, ANGLE_TARGET, CURRENT_ANGLE, EZLANDING, GPS_CONNECTION, GYRO_CALIBRATION, MAG_CALIB, MAG_TASK_RATE, RC_STATS and RPM_LIMIT came with features added after 4.4.3 (PRs #12231, #12094, #12799, #12241, #12998, #13166, #12978, #12054).
downgrade:debug-mode-new-modes-not-in-ta.note: This debug mode doesn't exist in 4.4.3, so your board's 4.4.3 default is used instead. Debug modes only change what goes into blackbox logs, so this doesn't affect flight. If you want logging, pick a mode that exists in 4.4.3, e.g. `set debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED`.

downgrade:failsafe-delay-min-clamped.detail: PR #13033 shortened the receiver signal recovery period from 200ms to 100ms, which lowered the minimum of failsafe_delay from 2 to 1 in 4.5.
downgrade:failsafe-delay-min-clamped.note: 4.4.3 doesn't accept a value of 1, so a value of 1 was raised to 2, the lowest 4.4.3 allows. All other values carry over unchanged.

downgrade:feedforward-max-rate-limit-cla.detail: PR #12605 widened the range from 0-150 to 0-200 and refined how the limit is applied: the value now sets the slope of the limiting line rather than shifting it. The default stays 90.
downgrade:feedforward-max-rate-limit-cla.note: 4.4.3 accepts values up to 150, so anything above 150 was lowered to 150. Values from 0 to 150 carry over unchanged.

downgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-range-cl.detail: PR #13047 changed the range from 2-255 to 5-1000 meters by moving the setting to a larger number type; the units stayed meters.
downgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-range-cl.note: 4.4.3 accepts return altitudes from 2 to 255 meters, so anything above 255 was lowered to 255. If you relied on a higher return altitude, check that 255 meters is suitable for where you fly.

downgrade:gps-ublox-models-merged-into-m.detail: PR #12587 split gps_ublox_mode into gps_ublox_acquire_model and gps_ublox_flight_model. The old DYNAMIC mode used pedestrian while acquiring and airborne in flight, so that pair maps back to DYNAMIC.
downgrade:gps-ublox-models-merged-into-m.note: 4.4.3 has a single gps_ublox_mode instead of separate acquire and flight models, so your two model settings were combined into the nearest mode: AIRBORNE, PEDESTRIAN or DYNAMIC. Models other than pedestrian and airborne (such as AUTOMOTIVE or PORTABLE) have no equivalent and end up as AIRBORNE.

downgrade:horizon-ignore-sticks-not-in-4.detail: PR #12231 replaced horizon_tilt_expert_mode with horizon_ignore_sticks and rewrote the Horizon algorithm. The new setting only turns off stick attenuation, while the old one switched to a different cutoff calculation.
downgrade:horizon-ignore-sticks-not-in-4.note: Nothing carries over to 4.4.3, because this setting does a different job from the Horizon setting 4.4.3 has in its place (horizon_tilt_expert_mode). 4.4.3 uses its own default for that setting, so check how Horizon mode feels before flying.

downgrade:horizon-level-strength-rescale.detail: PR #12231 rewrote Horizon mode. The gain changed from the value / 10 to the value / 100 (capped at 1), and it now scales an attitude- and stick-based attenuation factor instead of acting as a gain of its own. No formula maps values between the two versions.
downgrade:horizon-level-strength-rescale.note: Horizon self-levelling strength is scaled and applied differently in 4.4.3, so your value can't be converted and Horizon starts from the 4.4.3 default of 50. Fly Horizon and re-tune it, e.g. `set horizon_level_strength = 60` for stronger levelling. In 4.4.3 the range is 0-200.

downgrade:horizon-limit-degrees-not-in-4.detail: PR #12231 replaced horizon_tilt_effect with horizon_limit_degrees, a direct angle in degrees, inside a rewritten Horizon algorithm. The old setting was a 0-250 factor whose meaning depended on expert mode.
downgrade:horizon-limit-degrees-not-in-4.note: Nothing carries over to 4.4.3, because the units and the Horizon algorithm both changed. 4.4.3 uses its own default for its Horizon setting (horizon_tilt_effect), so check how Horizon mode feels before flying.

downgrade:horizon-limit-sticks-renamed-b.detail: PR #12231 renamed horizon_transition to horizon_limit_sticks for the same field. Its range went from 0-200 to 10-200, so every 4.5.5 value is also valid in 4.4.3.
downgrade:horizon-limit-sticks-renamed-b.note: Your Horizon mode stick limit carries over with the same value under its 4.4.3 name. Nothing to do. It still sets the stick deflection where self-levelling fades out completely.

downgrade:mag-hardware-mpu925x-entry-ren.detail: PR #12917 renamed the MAG_MPU925X_AK8963 compass entry to MPU925X_AK8963. 4.4.3 still uses the old name.
downgrade:mag-hardware-mpu925x-entry-ren.note: The compass choice MPU925X_AK8963 is called MAG_MPU925X_AK8963 in 4.4.3, so your value was renamed to match. It selects the same compass and you don't need to do anything.

downgrade:mag-hardware-new-sensors-not-i.detail: PR #12917 added the IST8310 compass and PR #13150 added the LIS2MDL, both after 4.4.3.
downgrade:mag-hardware-new-sensors-not-i.note: 4.4.3 doesn't support this magnetometer, so your board's own 4.4.3 magnetometer default is used instead. If you rely on the compass, check after flashing whether it is detected; there is no 4.4.3 driver for this sensor.

downgrade:mixer-type-ezlanding-not-in-ta.detail: PR #12094 added EZLANDING to the mixer_type list after LEGACY, LINEAR and DYNAMIC, along with its own mixer code. Versions before that change don't have it.
downgrade:mixer-type-ezlanding-not-in-ta.note: 4.4.3 has no EzLanding mixer mode and nothing equivalent, so the mixer runs as LEGACY, the 4.4.3 default, and you lose EzLanding's throttle-based landing behaviour. To use a different mixer, set it in the CLI, e.g. `set mixer_type = DYNAMIC` or `set mixer_type = LINEAR`.

downgrade:msp-override-failsafe-not-in-4.detail: PR #13380 added this setting so failsafe is not triggered when the correct roll, pitch, yaw and throttle values are sent via MSP_OVERRIDE.
downgrade:msp-override-failsafe-not-in-4.note: This option cannot be carried over, so the behaviour it controlled during MSP override is not available. If you use MSP override, check how failsafe behaves on the older firmware before flying.

downgrade:pinio-box-lap-timer-reset-unas.detail: PR #11856 added the GPS lap timer and its LAP TIMER RESET mode as mode ID 54. 4.4.3 has no mode with that ID, so it becomes 255, which means no mode.
downgrade:pinio-box-lap-timer-reset-unas.note: A PINIO output that was linked to the LAP TIMER RESET mode is set to 255 (unassigned), because 4.4.3 doesn't have that mode. All other PINIO mode links carry over unchanged. On 4.4.3 that pin won't follow any mode until you link it to another one.

downgrade:rpm-filter-weights-not-in-4-4.detail: PR #12838 added dimmable RPM harmonics, and PR #13172 raised the RPM filter config version.
downgrade:rpm-filter-weights-not-in-4-4.note: The per-harmonic RPM filter weights cannot be carried over, so the older firmware will use its own RPM filter behaviour. Re-check your RPM filter setup after the downgrade.

downgrade:rpm-limiter-not-in-4-4.detail: PR #12054 introduced the RPM limiter settings in 4.5, and none of them have a predecessor in 4.4.3.
downgrade:rpm-limiter-not-in-4-4.note: The RPM limiter is a 4.5 feature, so 4.4.3 has no limit on motor RPM and no setting to replace it. If you relied on the limit, the same protection is not available in 4.4.3.

downgrade:serialrx-provider-none-not-in-.detail: PR #12500 added NONE as the first serialrx_provider entry, replacing SPEK1024 as the default, and moved SPEK1024 further down the list. 4.4.3 comes before that change, so it has no NONE.
downgrade:serialrx-provider-none-not-in-.note: 4.4.3 has no NONE option for the serial receiver protocol, so your board's own 4.4.3 default protocol applies instead. If you use a serial receiver, set its protocol in the CLI, e.g. `set serialrx_provider = CRSF`.

downgrade:servo-endpoint-range-narrowed.note: Servo endpoint behavior is different in 4.4.3, and min or max values outside 750–2250 were narrowed into that range. Refer to https://github.com/betaflight/betaflight/pull/13451 for more information and verify servo behavior is as expected before flying.

upgrade:acc-hardware-fake-renamed-virtua.detail: PR #12493 renamed the FAKE accelerometer entry to VIRTUAL with no change in function.
upgrade:acc-hardware-fake-renamed-virtua.note: The accelerometer choice FAKE is called VIRTUAL in 4.5.5, so your value was renamed to match. It works the same way and you don't need to do anything.

upgrade:angle-level-strength-renamed-ang.note: Your value carries over unchanged as angle_p_gain. 4.5 now applies your acro rate curve to angle mode, which produces a very different stick feel. For instructions of how to revert this change, see https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t5UDq0fsImU

upgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-min-rais.detail: PR #13033 raised the minimum from 0 to 1 and changed the default from 10 to 5. PR #13215 sets the default to 1 on RACE_PRO builds.
upgrade:failsafe-recovery-delay-min-rais.note: The value is still in tenths of a second of valid receiver signal before failsafe recovery or arming is allowed. 0 is no longer allowed, so it becomes 1 (0.1 s). All other values carry over unchanged.

upgrade:gps-auto-baud-mostly-inactive.detail: In 4.4.3, ON made the flight controller cycle through baud rates after losing GPS communication. PR #12799 removed that code; the setting now only changes what the CLI `gps` status line shows.
upgrade:gps-auto-baud-mostly-inactive.note: Your value carries over, but gps_auto_baud has no effect in 4.5.5. Nothing to do.

upgrade:gps-rescue-max-angle-range-30-60.detail: PR #12854 changed the accepted range from 0-80 to 30-60. PR #12900 removed the groundspeed scaling, so GPS Rescue now always gets the full angle you set.
upgrade:gps-rescue-max-angle-range-30-60.note: The angle limit means the same thing in degrees, but it now has to be between 30 and 60. Values below 30 were raised to 30 and values above 60 were lowered to 60. Values already in that range are unchanged.

upgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-range-5-10.detail: PR #13047 changed the setting from an 8-bit value (2-255) to a 16-bit value (5-1000) and kept meters as the unit.
upgrade:gps-rescue-return-alt-range-5-10.note: The return altitude is still in meters, but it now has to be between 5 and 1000. A value of 2-4 was raised to 5. Any other value carries over unchanged.

upgrade:gps-ublox-acquire-model-from-mod.detail: PR #12587 split gps_ublox_mode into gps_ublox_acquire_model and gps_ublox_flight_model. The old firmware used the airborne model during acquisition only when the mode was AIRBORNE.
upgrade:gps-ublox-acquire-model-from-mod.note: The old GPS mode setting is now split into two settings. This one sets the model the GPS uses while it searches for satellites. It was filled in from your old mode: AIRBORNE became AIRBORNE_4G, and PEDESTRIAN or DYNAMIC became PEDESTRIAN, so the GPS works the same way it did before.

upgrade:gps-ublox-flight-model-from-mode.detail: PR #12587 split gps_ublox_mode into gps_ublox_acquire_model and gps_ublox_flight_model. The old firmware switched to the airborne model in flight for both AIRBORNE and DYNAMIC.
upgrade:gps-ublox-flight-model-from-mode.note: The old GPS mode setting is now split into two settings. This one sets the model the GPS uses in flight. It was filled in from your old mode: PEDESTRIAN stayed PEDESTRIAN, and AIRBORNE or DYNAMIC became AIRBORNE_4G, so the GPS works the same way it did before.

upgrade:horizon-level-strength-rescaled-.detail: PR #12231 rewrote Horizon mode. The gain changed from I/10 to I/100 (capped at 1), the range shrank from 0-200 to 0-100, and the gain now scales a new attenuation factor based on attitude and stick position.
upgrade:horizon-level-strength-rescaled-.note: Horizon's self-leveling strength now uses a different scale and works relative to the Angle mode settings, so your old value can't be converted. It is set to the 4.5.5 default of 75. Fly Horizon and adjust it if it doesn't feel right; to return to the default, use `set horizon_level_strength = 75`.

upgrade:horizon-tilt-effect-removed.detail: PR #12231 removed horizon_tilt_effect and its derived values and replaced them with horizon_limit_degrees inside a redesigned Horizon level calculation.
upgrade:horizon-tilt-effect-removed.note: Horizon mode was redesigned, and the new horizon_limit_degrees setting has a different meaning and units, so your old value can't be carried over. 4.5.5 uses its own default for horizon_limit_degrees; check how Horizon mode flies and adjust that setting if needed.

upgrade:horizon-tilt-expert-mode-removed.detail: PR #12231 removed horizon_tilt_expert_mode and its branches in the Horizon level calculation. horizon_ignore_sticks was added with a different function.
upgrade:horizon-tilt-expert-mode-removed.note: The old expert/non-expert tilt algorithm is gone, so there is nothing to carry over. The new horizon_ignore_sticks setting does something different, and 4.5.5 uses its own default for it; check Horizon mode behaviour after flashing.

upgrade:horizon-transition-renamed-limit.detail: PR #12231 renamed horizon_transition (range 0-200) to horizon_limit_sticks (range 10-200) on the same field. Both versions reach zero levelling at a stick deflection of value/100.
upgrade:horizon-transition-renamed-limit.note: Your Horizon-mode stick setting carries over under its new name and works the same way: self-levelling fades out completely at this stick deflection, in percent. The minimum is now 10, so values from 0 to 9 are raised to 10. If you used 0, check how Horizon mode feels after flashing.

upgrade:level-expo-removed.detail: PR #12231 removed roll_level_expo and pitch_level_expo. The Angle mode target angle is now angle_limit times the Acro setpoint divided by the maximum rate, so the rates curve replaces the level expo.
upgrade:level-expo-removed.note: Angle mode no longer has its own stick expo. In 4.5.5 it takes its stick feel from your Acro rates, so your rates curve now shapes how Angle mode responds to the sticks.

upgrade:level-limit-renamed-angle-limit-.detail: PR #12231 renamed level_limit (range 10-90, default 55) to angle_limit (range 10-85, default 60). It still sets the maximum Angle-mode angle in degrees.
upgrade:level-limit-renamed-angle-limit-.note: Your Angle-mode tilt limit carries over under its new name and still means the same thing: the maximum tilt in degrees at full stick. The new maximum is 85, so values from 86 to 90 are set to 85.

upgrade:mag-hardware-mpu925x-renamed.detail: PR #12917 renamed the MAG_MPU925X_AK8963 compass entry to MPU925X_AK8963 when it added IST8310 support.
upgrade:mag-hardware-mpu925x-renamed.note: The compass choice MAG_MPU925X_AK8963 is called MPU925X_AK8963 in 4.5.5, so your value was renamed to match. It selects the same compass and you don't need to do anything.

upgrade:servo-endpoint-range-widened.note: Servo endpoint behavior has changed. Refer to https://github.com/betaflight/betaflight/pull/13451 for more information and verify servo behavior is as expected before flying.

upgrade:tpa-breakpoint-range-1000-2000.detail: PR #12721 narrowed the range from 750-2250 to 1000-2000. The breakpoint is still worked out as (tpa_breakpoint - 1000)/1000 of throttle.
upgrade:tpa-breakpoint-range-1000-2000.note: The TPA breakpoint means the same thing, but it now has to be between 1000 and 2000. Values outside that range were moved to the nearest limit. Values already in that range are unchanged.

cmd:servo|downgrade|note:n2.comment: servo endpoint behavior differs in 4.4.3; see PR #13451 and verify servo behavior before flying

cmd:servo|upgrade|note:n1.comment: servo endpoint behavior has changed; see PR #13451 and verify servo behavior before flying

set:acc_hardware|downgrade|*.comment: VIRTUAL is called FAKE in 4.4.3, so the value was renamed; it works the same

set:acc_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: 4.4.3 has no LSM6DSV16X driver; set to AUTO. Check the accelerometer is detected after flashing

set:acc_hardware|upgrade|*.comment: FAKE is now called VIRTUAL, so the value was renamed; it works the same

set:angle_feedforward|upgrade|*.comment: New Angle-mode feedforward gain; it starts at its default of 50 and has no 4.4.3 equivalent.

set:angle_level_strength|upgrade|note:n1.comment: carries over unchanged as angle_p_gain; Angle mode now uses your Acro rate curve

set:angle_limit|upgrade|*.comment: renamed from level_limit with the same meaning in degrees; values above 85 are capped at 85

set:baro_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: this barometer choice isn't in 4.4.3; board default used. Check the baro is detected if you use it

set:debug_mode|downgrade|0.comment: this debug mode isn't in 4.4.3; board default used. Only affects blackbox logs, not flight

set:ez_landing_limit|upgrade|*.comment: New throttle-based EzLanding feature; it starts at its default of 15, with no 4.4.3 equivalent.

set:failsafe_delay|downgrade|*.comment: 4.4.3's minimum is 2, so a value of 1 becomes 2; other values are unchanged

set:failsafe_recovery_delay|upgrade|*.comment: the minimum is now 1 (0.1 s), so 0 becomes 1; other values carry over unchanged

set:feedforward_max_rate_limit|downgrade.comment: 4.4.3 allows at most 150, so higher values become 150; 0-150 carry over unchanged

set:gps_auto_baud|upgrade|note:n1.comment: carries over, but has no effect in 4.5.5; nothing to do

set:gps_rescue_max_angle|upgrade|*.comment: Same angle in degrees; now limited to 30-60, so values outside that range move to the nearest limit

set:gps_rescue_return_alt|downgrade|*.comment: 4.4.3 allows at most 255 meters, so higher values become 255; check it suits your flying area

set:gps_rescue_return_alt|upgrade|*.comment: Same meters; now limited to 5-1000, so a value of 2-4 becomes 5

set:gps_ublox_acquire_model|downgrade|*.comment: combined with the flight model into gps_ublox_mode, since 4.4.3 has no separate acquire model

set:gps_ublox_acquire_model|upgrade|*.comment: Filled in from your old GPS mode: AIRBORNE becomes AIRBORNE_4G, anything else becomes PEDESTRIAN

set:gps_ublox_flight_model|downgrade|*.comment: combined with the acquire model into gps_ublox_mode; models other than pedestrian/airborne become AIRBORNE

set:gps_ublox_flight_model|upgrade|*.comment: Filled in from your old GPS mode: PEDESTRIAN stays PEDESTRIAN, anything else becomes AIRBORNE_4G

set:gps_ublox_mode|downgrade|*.comment: set from your acquire and flight models; PEDESTRIAN acquire with airborne flight gives DYNAMIC

set:gps_update_rate_hz|upgrade|*.comment: New GPS update rate setting; 4.4.3 always used a fixed 10Hz, which matches the new default.

set:horizon_level_strength|downgrade|*.comment: Horizon strength is scaled differently in 4.4.3 (range 0-200); reset to 50, so re-tune Horizon

set:horizon_level_strength|upgrade|*.comment: Horizon strength has a new scale and can't be converted; set to default 75, re-tune in flight

set:horizon_limit_degrees|downgrade|*.comment: replaces horizon_tilt_effect with different units and algorithm, so nothing carries over

set:horizon_tilt_expert_mode|downgrade|*.comment: Tilt expert mode is the 4.4.3 Horizon algorithm option; nothing carries over, it stays OFF

set:horizon_tilt_expert_mode|upgrade|*.comment: Expert tilt algorithm is gone; horizon_ignore_sticks does something different, so nothing carries over

set:horizon_transition|downgrade|*.comment: 4.4.3 calls horizon_limit_sticks by this name; your value carries over unchanged

set:roll_level_expo|upgrade|*.comment: removed; Angle mode now takes its stick feel from your Acro rates

set:rpm_limit_i|downgrade|*.comment: RPM limiter I term; 4.4.3 has no RPM limiter

set:rpm_limit_p|downgrade|*.comment: RPM limiter P term; 4.4.3 has no RPM limiter

set:rpm_limit_value|downgrade|*.comment: RPM limit value; 4.4.3 has no RPM limiter, so no limit is applied

set:rpm_limit_value|upgrade|*.comment: New RPM limiter value setting in 4.5.5; its default depends on the board.

set:rpm_limit|downgrade|*.comment: RPM limiter on/off switch; 4.4.3 has no RPM limiter
